title: The sea was not the problem.
paragraphs: The sea was not the problem.
The fear was.

Imagine standing there…
Wind howling.
Salt in the air.
Children crying behind you.
War chariots roaring in the distance.
And the sea in front of you.

No bridge.
No boat.
No plan.
Just water.
This is the moment in Exodus 14 where Israel realizes something terrifying: freedom is real… but danger is still chasing them.
Egypt was behind them.
The Red Sea was in front of them.
And panic started spreading like wildfire.

Some people shouted.
Some people cried.
Some people blamed Moses.
“Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us to die in the wilderness?” (Exodus 14:11)
You can almost hear the bitterness.
This is what fear does.

Fear makes miracles feel small.
Fear makes yesterday’s deliverance look like a mistake.
Fear makes people want to go back to their chains just to feel safe.
Sound familiar?
How many times have we done the same thing?

God brings us out of something toxic…
But the moment life gets hard again, we start thinking about going back.

Back to the addiction.
Back to the relationship that broke us.
Back to the habits that slowly killed our soul.
Because the unknown feels scarier than the chains we recognize.
Israel stood there frozen.
And then Moses spoke one of the most powerful lines in Scripture.
“Fear ye not. Stand still. And see the salvation of the Lord.” (Exodus 14:13)
Let that sink in.
Stand.
Still.
Not run.
Not panic.
Not manipulate the situation.
Stand still.
Why?
Because the battle was never theirs to win.
And suddenly… the impossible happened.
God moved.
The wind began to roar across the sea.
The waters began to split.

Not a shallow puddle.
Not a symbolic moment.
A wall of water rose on both sides like towering blue mountains.
The seabed turned dry beneath their feet.
The place that looked like their grave became their escape route.
The sea didn’t disappear.
God made a path through it.
Read that again.
He didn’t remove the obstacle.
He opened a way inside the obstacle.
That is how God works.
Sometimes we pray for the sea to disappear.
But God says,
“No. I’m going to reveal My glory right in the middle of it.”
So Israel stepped forward.
Families walked between walls of water.
Mothers holding children.
Fathers guiding their people.
Hearts pounding.
But step by step, they crossed what should have drowned them.
And when the Egyptian army chased them into the same sea…
The waters collapsed.
The enemy that terrified them hours earlier was gone.
Forever.
And here is the deeper truth most people miss:
The Red Sea is more than history.
It is a preview of the Gospel.
Because humanity stood at its own impossible sea.

Sin behind us.
Judgment before us.
No amount of effort, religion, or morality could save us.
Then Jesus stepped into the story.
At the cross, He opened a path where none existed.
The wrath that should have swallowed us was poured out on Him.
And through His sacrifice, a way was made.
Not through water…
But through grace.
The Red Sea reminds us of something powerful:
God doesn’t just help you survive your enemies.
He destroys the power that chased you.
Your past does not get the final word.
Your shame does not get the final word.
Your failures do not get the final word.
Jesus does.
Maybe you feel like Israel right now.
Cornered.
Trapped.
No way forward.
Fear whispering that the story is over.
But listen carefully.
God specializes in impossible moments.
He still parts seas.
He still breaks chains.
He still writes redemption where everyone else sees a dead end.
Your Red Sea is not the end of the story.
It might be the place where God is about to show His greatest power.
So don’t turn back to Egypt.
Don’t surrender to fear.
Stand still.
Trust the Lord.
And watch what He does next.
“The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.” (Exodus 14:14)
Someone in your circle may be standing at their own Red Sea right now.
And they need to know:
God still makes a way where there is no way.
